description: tests/common/mod.rs: Inner.objects, Inner.states, and Inner.change_log are all HashMap<(String, String), ...> keyed by (type_name, account_id). These are stringly-typed keys — swapping the order silently compiles. The idiomatic Rust approach is a newtype or a small struct: struct StoreKey { type_name: &'static str, account_id: String } or an enum for type_name. More importantly, current_state(), bump_state(), objects_mut(), and objects_ref() all construct (type_name.to_owned(), account_id.to_owned()) inline — allocating a new String for type_name on every call even though TYPE_NAME is &'static str. Using (&'static str, &str) as the lookup key with Borrow<(&'static str, str)> or using a two-level HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<String, ...>> would eliminate these allocations. This is test code but it is also the canonical MailBackend example — implementors copy these patterns.
title: MemoryBackend inner state uses (String, String) tuple keys — should be typed
